tristan-harris.quote: And, of course, this is emerging out of human choice, and there are examples in human history where we’ve chosen just not to build something.

tristan-harris.position: He favours steering AI development carefully rather than stopping AI altogether.
tristan-harris.quote: we're not advocating no AI or bad, you're gonna stop ai. We're advocating for pro steering.
tristan-harris.work: The Great Simplification ep. 214: Tristan Harris (transcript)

tristan-harris.position: Managing AI's competitive dynamics requires international coordination, not only national laws.
tristan-harris.quote: And it does need to be coordination because national laws as big as they are and as hard as they are to accomplish, won't get you all the way to this competitive dynamic.
tristan-harris.work: The Great Simplification ep. 214: Tristan Harris (transcript)

tristan-harris.position: Technology should be designed to support the social fabric and the natural world it depends on.
tristan-harris.quote: humane technology has always meant technology that is humane to the underlying, sort of society substrate biosphere upon which it is, it depends and needs to surf.
tristan-harris.work: The Great Simplification ep. 214: Tristan Harris (transcript)

tristan-harris.position: Engagement-optimised social media was an early, misaligned AI that harmed mental health and democracy.
tristan-harris.quote: So, you know, if a baby AI could do that, and that was a misaligned ai right?
tristan-harris.work: The Great Simplification ep. 214: Tristan Harris (transcript)

tyler-cowen.position: AI will transform the world over decades but raise growth only modestly each year, about half a percentage point.
tyler-cowen.quote: I think they will boost the rate of economic growth by something like half a percentage point a year. Over 30-40 years, that's an enormous difference. It will transform the entire world.
tyler-cowen.work: Tyler Cowen — The #1 bottleneck to AI progress is humans

tyler-cowen.position: Human and institutional bottlenecks, not machine intelligence, set the pace of AI's economic impact.
tyler-cowen.quote: Human bottlenecks become more important, the more productive is AI.
tyler-cowen.work: Why I think AI take-off is relatively slow

tyler-cowen.position: Long-run effects of radical technologies cannot be foreseen, so radical agnosticism about specific AI scenarios is appropriate.
tyler-cowen.quote: Radical agnosticism is the correct response, where all specific scenarios are pretty unlikely.
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

tyler-cowen.position: Halting AI is not a real option because the previous era of stability is ending anyway.
tyler-cowen.quote: So there is no “ongoing stasis” option on the table.
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

tyler-cowen.position: Alignment research is worth supporting as ordinary improvement of a technology.
tyler-cowen.quote: Nonetheless I am still for people doing constructive work on the problem of alignment, just as we do with all other technologies, to improve them.
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

tyler-cowen.position: Writers should now treat AI systems as a major audience for their work.
tyler-cowen.quote: I'm happy if humans read it, but mostly I wrote it for the AIs.
tyler-cowen.work: Tyler Cowen — The #1 bottleneck to AI progress is humans

venkatesh-rao.position: Fears of superintelligent AI rest on ill-posed, anthropomorphic concepts such as general intelligence and sentience.
venkatesh-rao.quote: I will call the terms in this list pseudo-traits.

venkatesh-rao.position: Modern AI is better seen as a discovery about computational reality than as an invention or machine.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The word we’re looking for is discovery.

venkatesh-rao.position: Humans and AI are entering a symbiosis comparable to the evolutionary origin of complex cells.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The emergence of AI, in the particular form that it has appeared (deep learning), is arguably the eukaryotic moment in human cultural evolution, understood in memetic terms, with humans playing the role of mitochondria, and AI the role of the nucleus.

venkatesh-rao.position: No single moral movement or faction should settle the meaning and governance of AI for everyone.
venkatesh-rao.quote: No faction should get to settle the moral meaning of AI for everyone else, or act unilaterally and pre-emptively to foreclose particular futures for all.

venkatesh-rao.position: Cheap AI can let most people become consumers of intelligence rather than making them economically redundant.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The analogous possibility with AI is that most people will no longer need to be significant producers of intelligence in order to become significant consumers of it.

venkatesh-rao.position: AI should be governed through protocols, contracts and bounded authority rather than permanent human control.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The choice is not between human control and machine control. It is between domination and symbiosis.

vitalik-buterin.position: Technology should be accelerated selectively toward defense and away from concentrating power.
vitalik-buterin.quote: Build technologies that shift the offense/defense balance toward defense, and do so in a way that does not rely on handing over more power to centralized authorities.

vitalik-buterin.position: Transformative technology can make the future much better than the present.
vitalik-buterin.quote: I believe in a future that is vastly brighter than the present thanks to radically transformative technology, and I believe in humans and humanity.

vitalik-buterin.position: The direction of technological development matters, not only its speed.
vitalik-buterin.quote: However, I think that not just magnitude but also direction matters.

vitalik-buterin.position: Centralized control for safety carries its own risks; decentralized approaches handle them better.
vitalik-buterin.quote: A decentralized approach would better address risks from the center itself.

vitalik-buterin.position: Defensive technology can make AI takeover scenarios much less likely to succeed.
vitalik-buterin.quote: Rather, my view is that the "endgame" of cybersecurity is very defense-favoring, and with the kinds of rapid technology development that AI 2027 assumes, we can get there.

william-macaskill.position: AI that can do research is likely to compress a century of technological progress into about a decade.
william-macaskill.quote: it is in fact likely that advanced AI will drive a hundred years’ worth of technological development in less than a decade.

william-macaskill.position: Preparing for advanced AI means handling many grand challenges, not only aligning AI systems.
william-macaskill.quote: AGI preparedness is therefore not just about ensuring that advanced AI systems are aligned: we should be preparing, now, for the disorienting range of developments an intelligence explosion would bring.

william-macaskill.position: Making good futures better deserves roughly as much priority as avoiding catastrophe.
william-macaskill.quote: This essay series will argue that work on Flourishing is in the same ballpark of priority as work on Surviving.

william-macaskill.position: Society should aim for a state that can steer itself toward good outcomes rather than toward one fixed ideal future.
william-macaskill.quote: From my point of view, the key priority in the world today is to get us closer to viatopia, not to some particular narrow end-state.

william-macaskill.position: The character AI systems are given will strongly shape society, so deciding it carefully is a top priority.
william-macaskill.quote: We think that figuring out what characters AI systems should have, and getting companies to actually build them that way, is among the most valuable things that people can do today.

william-macaskill.position: Effective altruism should make the transition to a post-AGI society a major focus.
william-macaskill.quote: I argue for a third way: EA should embrace the mission of making the transition to a post-AGI society go well, significantly expanding our cause area focus beyond traditional AI safety.
william-macaskill.work: Effective altruism in the age of AGI

william-saunders.position: Decisions that impose large risks on the world should be made with broad, legitimate authority, not by companies alone.
william-saunders.quote: Principle 1: Seek as broad and legitimate authority for your decisions as is possible under the circumstances

william-saunders.position: No one should impose significant risks on others without strong evidence that benefits clearly outweigh them.
william-saunders.quote: Principle 2: Don’t take actions which impose significant risks to others without overwhelming evidence of net benefit

william-saunders.position: Independent experts without conflicts of interest should check whether AI companies have done enough safety work.
william-saunders.quote: the only way I can see is independent experts who have access to see what is actually being done and who can actually make this call without having a massive conflict of interest.
william-saunders.work: Former OpenAI Engineer William Saunders on Silence, Safety, and the Right to Warn

william-saunders.position: AI employees need protected channels to raise risk concerns with boards, regulators and independent bodies.
william-saunders.quote: That the company will facilitate a verifiably anonymous process for current and former employees to raise risk-related concerns to the company’s board, to regulators, and to an appropriate independent organization with relevant expertise;
william-saunders.work: My Perspective On "A Right to Warn about Advanced Artificial Intelligence"

william-saunders.position: Frontier AI should combine tight security on replicable technology with required transparency on safety and capabilities.
william-saunders.quote: I advocate for both tight security and more transparency, which might seem contradictory

william-saunders.position: Making advanced AI safe is achievable if developers are willing to do the hard work.
william-saunders.quote: I do think we can figure this technology out. I do think we can do it properly. I think that is totally possible, but we have to be willing to put in the hard work to do that.
william-saunders.work: Former OpenAI Engineer William Saunders on Silence, Safety, and the Right to Warn

yann-lecun.position: Language models trained on text lack understanding of the physical world, persistent memory, reasoning and planning, so new architectures are needed.
yann-lecun.quote: LLMs can do none of those or they can only do them in a very primitive way and they don’t really understand the physical world.
yann-lecun.work: Transcript for Yann LeCun: Meta AI, Open Source, Limits of LLMs, AGI & the Future of AI

yann-lecun.position: A system trained on language alone cannot reach human-level intelligence, because most knowledge is not linguistic.
yann-lecun.quote: A system trained on language alone will never approximate human intelligence, even if trained from now until the heat death of the universe.
yann-lecun.work: AI And The Limits Of Language

yann-lecun.position: Foundational AI should be open source because it is becoming shared infrastructure for communication.
yann-lecun.quote: AI has to be open source because we need a common infrastructure when a platform is becoming an essential part of the fabric of communication.
yann-lecun.work: How Not to Be Stupid About AI, With Yann LeCun

yann-lecun.position: Human-level AI will arrive through gradual progress, not a single sudden event.
yann-lecun.quote: It’s not going to be an event. It’s going to be gradual progress.
yann-lecun.work: Transcript for Yann LeCun: Meta AI, Open Source, Limits of LLMs, AGI & the Future of AI

yann-lecun.position: Misuse is best countered by faster open progress, so that well-intentioned AI stays ahead of badly-intentioned AI.
yann-lecun.quote: Then it’s my good AI against your bad AI. The way to stay ahead is to progress faster.
yann-lecun.work: How Not to Be Stupid About AI, With Yann LeCun

yann-lecun.position: AI assistants will amplify human intelligence, much as the printing press did.
yann-lecun.quote: So AI is going to make humanity smarter.
yann-lecun.work: Transcript for Yann LeCun: Meta AI, Open Source, Limits of LLMs, AGI & the Future of AI

yoshua-bengio.position: No one currently knows how to make AGI or superintelligent AI reliably behave as intended.
yoshua-bengio.quote: while we are racing towards AGI or even ASI, nobody currently knows how such an AGI or ASI could be made to behave morally, or at least behave as intended by its developers and not turn against humans.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: Deep uncertainty about AI's future calls for humility and the precautionary principle.
yoshua-bengio.quote: rational decision-making calls for humility, recognizing our epistemic uncertainty and following scientific decision theory, which leads to the precautionary principle.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: No single person, company or government should be able to abuse the power of advanced AI.
yoshua-bengio.quote: We need to make sure that no single human, no single corporation and no single government can abuse the power of AGI at the expense of the common good.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: The safest AI would have no agency: it would understand the world without pursuing goals.
yoshua-bengio.quote: In fact, as I argue here, the safest kind of AI I can imagine is one with no agency at all, only a scientific understanding of the world (which could already be immensely useful).

yoshua-bengio.position: International treaties, including verification through chip hardware, are worth pursuing to prevent global AI catastrophe.
yoshua-bengio.quote: Even if it is not sure that they would work, they seem like an important avenue to explore to avoid a globally catastrophic outcome.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: If control and coordination problems are solved, advanced AI could greatly benefit humanity.
yoshua-bengio.quote: if both the AI control problem and the AI coordination problem are solved, I buy the argument that there is a good chance that humanity could benefit immensely from the scientific and technological advances that could follow
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yuval-noah-harari.position: AI differs from earlier technologies because it can make decisions and create ideas by itself.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: AI is radically different from previous technologies because it can make decisions and create ideas by itself.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Artificial Intelligence: A Guest Post by Yuval Noah Harari

yuval-noah-harari.position: By mastering language, AI gains power over the culture that human institutions rest on.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: AI has thereby hacked the operating system of our civilisation.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Watch out humans: AI has hacked the operating system of civilisation

yuval-noah-harari.position: AI should be legally required to disclose that it is an AI.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: And the first regulation I would suggest is to make it mandatory for AI to disclose that it is an AI.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Watch out humans: AI has hacked the operating system of civilisation

yuval-noah-harari.position: Humans can keep control of AI only if they cooperate and trust one another.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: Together, humans can control AI. But if we fight one another, AI will control us.
yuval-noah-harari.work: AI and the Paradox of Trust (China Development Forum speech)

yuval-noah-harari.position: New technologies often cause historical disasters while people learn to use them wisely.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: Novel technology often leads to historical disasters, not because the technology is inherently bad, but because it takes time for humans to learn how to use it wisely.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Why AI poses an existential danger to humanity

yuval-noah-harari.position: The main risk from AI is that humans lose control over it.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: The main risk is that we will lose control over this technology.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Artificial Intelligence: A Guest Post by Yuval Noah Harari

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Sincere disagreements about AI mostly come down to different expectations about what future AI will be able to do.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: Sincere disagreements about AI are usually disagreements about future AI capabilities.

zvi-mowshowitz.position: AI will likely become better than humans at almost everything within our lifetimes.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: I am ASI pilled. A large percentage of employees of the frontier labs are ASI pilled. The labs themselves are ASI pilled.

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Superintelligence should not be built until the risk of human extinction and loss of control is very low.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: We should not build superintelligence until such time as that changes, and the risk of everyone dying as a result, as well as the risk of losing control over the future as a result, is very low.
zvi-mowshowitz.work: New Statement Calls For Not Building Superintelligence For Now

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Low-cost safety measures such as oversight, transparency, liability and testing should be adopted now.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: There is no good case for not doing radically more investment in alignment, infrastructure and oversight, state capacity, transparency, liability, disclosures, safety testing including of internal models

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Patching and monitoring misaligned models is not a lasting fix; the underlying alignment problem must be solved.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: If you use iterative development to spot the underlying problem, it can work. If you use iterative development to patch the marginal issue over and over, then you are sitting on a time bomb.

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Society should build the ability to slow frontier AI development before it is needed.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: Thus, we collectively need to assess our situation, increase our ability to steer gracefully, and be ready to adjust our pace.
